document.abstract: This paper describes the development of an Intranet scene preview capability within Warner Bros. Feature Animation. This capability was developed so all members of the production staff could easily view production material as it was being animated. The animation production process as it pertains to the preview capabilities is presented and the organization of the server is reviewed. A discussion of HyperText MarkUp Language (HTML) along with the structure and function of the custom software developed is given. Performance and enhancements of QuickTime downloading and playback is also discussed.

authors.bio: Leonard Reder is currently with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory California Institute of Technology implementing astronomical interferometers. His interests include realtime image and DSP processing for scientific instrumentation, video and film post-production technologies, and software development techniques. Reder was formally with Warner Bros. Feature Animation from 1996 to 1999 and was the principal software engineer assigned to the editorial and post-production departments. His main responsibilities included developing infrastructure applications for integrating nonlinear editing systems, film recorders, and the screening room into the production animation process. Reder is a member of the SMPTE working group on editorial procedures and practices. He earned a MSEE degree from the University of Southern California and a B.S. in electronic engineering from Cal Poly University at San Luis Obispo.

authors.bio: Gene Takahashi works at Pixar Animation Studios and provides technical support for the editorial departments. He also runs his own company, Multimedia Audio Productions, which specializes in audio and music editing. His interests include audio, video, music, and film production as well as writing. Previously, Takahashi was employed with Warner Bros. Feature Animation where he was involved in the setup and technical operations of the studio. Takahashi has published technical articles in various trade publications. He holds a B.A. and M.A. degree in music as well as associate degrees in electronics and in the recording arts.
